what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is a technique that lets a cloud server compute on data that remains encrypted the entire time — the server never sees the raw numbers. This is extremely powerful for privacy, but FHE operations involve huge mathematical objects (encrypted numbers called ciphertexts) that are orders of magnitude larger than ordinary data, making FHE brutally slow even on dedicated chips. A key bottleneck is the cost of moving those large ciphertexts between the processor and main memory chips (DRAM — large but slow off-chip storage). FHENDI attacks this by moving the computation closer to the memory: specialized arithmetic units are placed directly inside or adjacent to the DRAM chips, so data barely has to travel. The design exploits four levels of parallelism in FHE computations, routes data cleverly to avoid conflicts within the memory chip, and uses a compiler to pipeline multiple encryption operations so no unit sits idle.
